title: KV cache mosaic rechunker and spillback policy (tenant-aware defragmentation)
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation from variable-sized entries and incremental spills was causing increased resident set size and p95 latency spikes under mixed workloads. Small free holes accumulate and cause frequent paging/spillovers despite overall available capacity. This PR introduces a tenant-aware background defragmenter ("mosaic rechunker") plus a controlled spillback policy to an asynchronous compressed spill pool to lower fragmentation and reduce tail latencies while keeping steady-state throughput. Summary of changes: 1) mosaic rechunker: a background worker that identifies small adjacent free slots and coalesces live objects into compact segments, using a lightweight pinning protocol to avoid KV reads during relocation. The worker uses tenant affinity and request-rate heuristics to prioritize cold tenants and minimize user impact. 2) spillback manager: when memory pressure is sustained above a configurable threshold, large cold segments are asynchronously compressed and written to the spill pool (on-disk/remote SSD) with eviction tickets. Spillback is rate-limited and can be configured per-tenant; the runtime can transparently fetch and rehydrate segments on demand. 3) scheduler integration: the serving scheduler receives new kernel hints so hot-path token-generation requests avoid nodes with active rehousing operations; background rechunker and spill tasks are throttled by runtime SLO tokens to limit tail impact. 4) observability and safety: added telemetry events for rechunk steps, spillback latencies, and per-tenant reclaimed bytes; added graceful shutdown and abort semantics for in-flight relocations. Checklist: - [x] mosaic rechunker prototype and unit tests - [x] spillback manager and integration tests with simulated remote pool - [x] scheduler kernel hints and integration with continuous batching - [x] perf harness and benchmarks showing improvements - [x] ops doc with tuning knobs and recommended thresholds Results (perf harness, mixed RW with realistic doc sizes): - Median latency for small gen requests: ~2.8ms -> 2.6ms (3.6% improvement) - P95 latency for mixed workload: 44ms -> 31ms (29.5% improvement) - Resident set memory fragmentation reduced by ~28% across tenants - Steady-state throughput unchanged within 1-2% (no regression) Backwards compatibility and flags: feature gated behind runtime flag kv.rechunk.enabled=false by default; spillback requires kv.spillback.enabled=false to opt-in. Migration: non-disruptive. See docs/ops/kv-rechunker.md for tuning guidance and recommended defaults. Motivation references: ENG-2345 (fragmentation incidents), SUP-891 (support ticket describing tenant OOM while node had free holes).
commits: a1f9c8b: Add mosaic rechunker scaffolding and relocation protocol
b3d2f7e: Implement spillback manager with compression pipeline and eviction tickets
c4e6b12: Expose scheduler kernel hints and SLO token gating for background work
d5a7c3f: Tests, perf harness integration, and ops doc
review_comments: Ethan Cole: The relocation protocol looks solid but we need a stronger invariant around multi-threaded pin/unpin to avoid ABA; please add a stress test for concurrent relocations.
Marta Lopez: Can we add a per-tenant hard cap on concurrent spillback streams? A single noisy tenant shouldn't saturate the remote pool.
Samir Gupta: The scheduler hint interface is small and safe, but please ensure hint propagation doesn't add RPC overhead on the hot path; consider caching decisions for 100ms.
Priya Nair (author): Added stress test and fixed pin/unpin ABA window; implemented tenant-level concurrent spillback cap. Scheduler hint now cached for 150ms by default and feature-gated.
release_notes: Introduces an experimental kv.rechunk background defragmenter and kv.spillback remote compressed spill policy. Reduces KV cache fragmentation and p95 tail latencies for mixed workloads. Feature-gated; see docs/ops/kv-rechunker.md for tuning.
